question: v12
q: Do landlords pay more than owner-occupiers on a standard variable loan?

transcript.answer:
Yes. In **September 2026** the banks' advertised standard variable rate was **9.35% for investors and 8.77% for owner-occupiers**, so landlords were paying **0.58 percentage points more**.

**The gap hasn't changed:** it was 0.58 points every month from January 2025 to September 2026. Both rates moved together with each cash rate change:

| Period | Owner-occupier | Investor | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan 2025 | 8.77% | 9.35% | 0.58 |
| Aug 2025 – Jan 2026 (low point) | 8.02% | 8.60% | 0.58 |
| May – Sep 2026 | 8.77% | 9.35% | 0.58 |

**What it costs:** on a $500,000 balance, 0.58 points works out to about **$2,900 a year** in extra interest for an investor, before any tax deductions.

These are the banks' **advertised standard rates** from RBA table F5. Most borrowers get a discount, so the rates people actually pay on new loans are lower. Investors still usually pay more than owner-occupiers, but the actual gap could be different. I can look up the rates actually paid on loans (RBA table F6) if you want that comparison.
